subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's internal yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context event-loop stalls despite possible extra-bootstrap ordering, prompt-byte, and session-timing changes?
rationale: The patch is a focused, well-tested fix for a live P1 stall, but it changes bootstrap file loading and hook scheduling on a compatibility-sensitive prompt/session path where automation should not unilaterally accept the upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
options.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, refresh exact-head checks if needed, and land this as the focused fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87509.

options.title: Request One More Live Run
options.body: Ask for a current-head embedded-run or channel-latency transcript showing bootstrap-context no longer stalls channel I/O before accepting the compatibility risk.

options.title: Pause For Architecture Work
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it if maintainers want this bottleneck solved through worker isolation, priority queues, caching, or lazy loading instead of this mitigation.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
recommendation.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, refresh exact-head checks if needed, and land this as the focused fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87509.
